cards.front: Recall a key point about Folding, Faulting & Geological Structures
cards.back: Folds: anticlines (upfolds), synclines (downfolds), overfolds and recumbent folds, formed by compression

cards.front: Recall a key point about Folding, Faulting & Geological Structures
cards.back: Faults: normal (tension), reverse/thrust (compression), strike-slip (shear), identified by displacement of rock layers

cards.front: Recall a key point about Folding, Faulting & Geological Structures
cards.back: Joints: fractures with no movement, formed by cooling (igneous) or tectonic stress; columnar jointing in basalt

cards.front: Recall a key point about Folding, Faulting & Geological Structures
cards.back: Unconformities: angular (tilted older rocks overlain by younger horizontal beds), disconformity (parallel beds with erosion gap), nonconformity (igneous/metamorphic overlain by sedimentary)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Folding, Faulting & Geological Structures
cards.back: Hutton's unconformity at Siccar Point was key evidence for deep time and the principle of uniformitarianism

cards.front: Recall a key point about Folding, Faulting & Geological Structures
cards.back: In the field, structures are identified by bedding plane orientation, displacement, and map patterns

cards.back: 1. For Folding, Faulting & Geological Structures questions, use correct geological terminology and classify features precisely 2.
